issues.failure_explanation: The proof expands ||gamma(s)-(X+sV)||_F^2 into only even powers s^4, s^6, ..., i.e. it treats the coefficients A_2, A_3, ... of s^2, s^3, ... in gamma(s)-(X+sV) as mutually orthogonal. They are not: for d>=3 the order-s^2 term G x_j du_j x_k du_k x_{l!=j,k} u_l (from the second part of gamma) and the order-s^3 term C x_j [du_j 0] x_k [du_k 0] x_{l!=j,k} [u_l u_{l,1}] (from the first part) occupy the same mode subspaces (modes j,k in du-directions, the remaining modes containing u_l-directions), so their inner product is generically nonzero; e.g. rank-one aligned C and G give exactly parallel terms with inner product gc||du_j||^2||du_k||^2 != 0. Hence the squared norm contains odd-power terms such as 2s^5<A_2,A_3>, and the displayed identity, on which the subsequent inequalities are built, is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Pythagorean-style expansion by a triangle bound ||gamma(s)-(X+sV)|| <= sum_m s^m ||A_m||, estimating each A_m via ||du_k||_2 <= ||V||/sigma_min(X) and ||du_k G_(k)||_F <= ||V|| together with s||V|| <= 1; this proves the lemma with an enlarged d-dependent factor in c(X), and all downstream results survive with adjusted constants.
issues.overall_effect: The curvature estimate (eq: curvature) is unproven as written. prop: backtracking GRAP uses it for the stepsize lower bound, and prop: GRAP-R decrease and thm: GRAP-R (apocalypse-freeness of GRAP-R) are built on that proposition, so the entire GRAP-R convergence chain rests on an invalid computation.
issues.title: False even-power expansion in the proof of the curvature bound (lem:added-1)
issues.why_classification: The lemma's final bound appears true and generous (numerical tests and crude estimates confirm it), but its proof rests on a false identity, and repairing it requires abandoning the even-power decomposition for a different, contained estimate. No claim, regime, or rate is lost, only constants: moderate, not minor (a nontrivial replacement argument is needed) and not serious.

issues.failure_explanation: By prop: backtracking GRAP the guaranteed stepsize is min{rho(1-a)/a_tilde, rho*bar_s}, and its hypothesis bar_s <= min{1/||V_X||,1} forces the effective initial stepsize in the application to at most min{bar_s, 1/||V_X||, 1}, so the correct lower bound contains the entry rho*bar_s. The displayed bound replaces this entry by rho, which is valid only if bar_s >= min{1, 1/||V_X||}; in particular under the proposition's own hypothesis bar_s <= 1 one has rho*bar_s <= rho, so the displayed inequality is false whenever bar_s < min{1, 1/||V_X||}. The same unjustified 'rho' entry propagates into the definitions of delta(underline{X}) in cases 1-3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the 'rho' entry by 'rho*bar_s' (or rho*min{bar_s,1}) in the displayed minima and in the definitions of delta(underline{X}); the deltas then acquire a fixed positive factor bar_s and every subsequent conclusion is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The constants delta(underline{X}) claimed in prop: GRAP-R decrease are unsupported as written (they can overestimate the guaranteed one-step decrease), so the sufficient-decrease condition and the contradiction argument in thm: GRAP-R inherit an unjustified step.
issues.title: Stepsize lower bound in prop: GRAP-R decrease drops the line-search parameter bar{s}
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction of a constant with trivial propagation (delta scaled by the fixed algorithm parameter bar_s); all claims and guarantees are preserved, so the least severe complete resolution is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We prove the result by contradiction. Suppose that there is a subsequence $\{\tensX^{(t_j)}\}_{j=0}^{\infty}$ converging to a non-stationary point $\underline{\tensX}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts that finite termination of alg: GRAP-R yields a stationary point, but the algorithm's stopping criteria are never specified, so nothing in the source links loop exit to stationarity (with arbitrary criteria the algorithm could stop anywhere). The proof of thm: GRAP-R addresses only the infinite case via a contradiction argument on a convergent subsequence, so the finite-termination clause is a promise not established by the paper. thm:added-1 repeats the identical clause for alg: rfGRAP-R, proved 'in a same fashion'.

failure_location.quote: If $\{\tensX^{(t)}\}$ is finite, the~\cref{alg: GRAP-R} terminates at a stationary point.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the stopping criterion (e.g. terminate when the computed search direction vanishes, which then implies stationarity through the angle conditions of prop: angle condition GRAP and prop: approximate rfGRAP), or qualify/drop the finite-termination clauses of thm: GRAP-R and thm:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-termination guarantee of thm: GRAP-R and thm:added-1 is not established; the accumulation-point (apocalypse-freeness) guarantees are unaffected by this issue.
issues.title: Finite-termination clause of thm: GRAP-R is unsupported (stopping criteria unspecified)
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence repair (fixing the natural stopping criterion or weakening the clause) preserves all substantive convergence guarantees; only an unproven side clause about the finite case is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider $\breve{\vecr}=(\breve{r}_1,\breve{r}_2,\dots,\breve{r}_d)$ with $\breve{r}_k=\min\{r_k-1,\rank(\matx_{(k)})\}$ for $k\in I$ and $\breve{r}_k=r_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$.

it follows from~\cref{prop: rank delta} that $\rank_\Delta(\matx_{(k)})\leq\underline{r}_k\leq\rank(\matx_{(k)})$ for all $k\in I$ and $\rank(\matx_{(k)})=r_k=\underline{r}_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$

issues.failure_explanation: Three linked gaps. (a) The stated epsilon(underline{X}) contains no sigma_min(underline{X}) term, so the claims underline{r}_k <= rank(x_(k)) and rank(x_(k)) = r_k on [d]\I -- needed both for the candidate breve{r} to lie in the algorithm's index sets (eq: rfGRAP index) and for the HOSVD proximity bound -- do not follow from prop: rank delta (nearby feasible X can have lower mode ranks); the parallel GRAP-R proof does include this term. (b) The candidate X_breve{r} generically has Tucker rank breve{r} with breve{r}_k up to r_k-1, not underline{r}; applying lem: inequality at that point yields the product prod_{k in I}(r_k - breve{r}_k)/min{n_k,n_{-k}}, which is strictly smaller than the claimed c_I = prod_{k in I}(r_k - underline{r}_k)/min{n_k,n_{-k}} whenever breve{r}_k > underline{r}_k (which occurs whenever the current iterate has mode rank above underline{r}_k), so the displayed bound with sqrt(c_I) uses the lemma outside its hypotheses. (c) The asserted continuity ||tilde{P}_k(nabla f(X_breve{r}))|| >= (1/2)||tilde{P}_k(nabla f(underline{X}))|| for all k in [d] is false in general: for deficient modes the candidate's unfolding carries breve{r}_k - underline{r}_k additional near-null singular directions, and components of tilde{P}_k(nabla f(underline{X})) lying in those directions are annihilated by the projection onto the complement of breve{u}_k.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Repair case 2 of prop: rfGRAP: add the term (1/(2(sqrt(d)+1)))sigma_min(underline{X}) to epsilon(underline{X}) as in the GRAP-R proof; apply lem: inequality at the candidate with its own rank, replacing sqrt(c_I) by the uniform bound prod_{k in I} sqrt(1/min{n_k,n_{-k}}); and replace the all-k continuity claim by the valid transfers (full modes k not in I, where the candidate's bases do converge, and the first candidate tilde{P}_0), bounding ||V_underline{X}|| through the decomposition of non-stationarity into the negations of conditions (i)/(ii). The proposition and thm:added-1 then hold with smaller constants.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient decrease condition for rfGRAP-R at non-stationary, non-full-rank accumulation points is unproven as written, so the convergence guarantee thm:added-1 for rfGRAP-R (one of the paper's two advertised apocalypse-free methods) is unsupported until the case-2 analysis is repaired.
issues.title: Case-2 analysis of prop: rfGRAP applies rank-underline{r} bounds at the higher-rank candidate X_breve{r}
issues.why_classification: The result is plausibly true and repairable with tools already in the source (uniform angle-condition constants, the max-structure of the partial projection, rank-dependent products), but the repair is a contained yet genuinely nontrivial rederivation of the key lower bounds; no claim, regime, or guarantee type must be abandoned, so it is moderate rather than serious.
